title: SIC-Agents: Benchmarking and Building an Adaptive Simulator for Pediatric Serious Illness Communication Training
abstract: arXiv:2608.29481v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Pediatric serious illness communication (SIC) is critically important, yet scalable communication training for clinicians remains limited. Compared with other dialogue simulation settings, pediatric SIC poses additional challenges, including multi-party interactions, response to parental distress and strong dependence on feedback dynamics. Existing LLM-based simulators optimize generic dialogue quality rather than curriculum-contingent behavior required for effective SIC training. translated_title: SIC-Agents：面向儿科重症疾病沟通训练的基准测试与自适应模拟器构建
translated_abstract: 儿科重症疾病沟通（SIC）至关重要，但面向临床医生的可扩展沟通训练仍然有限。与其他对话模拟场景相比，儿科SIC带来了额外的挑战，包括多方互动、对家长痛苦情绪的回应以及对反馈动态的强依赖。现有的基于大语言模型（LLM）的模拟器优化的是通用对话质量，而非有效的SIC训练所需的依赖课程的行为。我们与教育工作者和儿科临床医生合作，推出了首个专为儿科SIC训练定制的基准测试套件和模拟框架。我们的基准测试——PitfallBench和DialogueBench——从轮次级别和完整对话两个层面评估模拟器。我们进一步提出了SIC-Agents，这是一个自我改进的框架，可生成由临床医生编辑的技能文档来指导模拟器行为。我们的实验表明，SIC-Agents优于现有方法（摘要原文在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文与教育工作者和儿科临床医生合作，推出了首个针对儿科重症疾病沟通训练的基准测试套件（PitfallBench和DialogueBench），并提出自我改进框架SIC-Agents，通过生成临床医生可编辑的技能文档来指导模拟器行为，其性能优于现有方法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the first benchmark suite (PitfallBench and DialogueBench) and a self-improving framework called SIC-Agents for pediatric serious illness communication training, which generates a clinician-editable skill document to guide simulator behavior and outperforms existing methods.
